memories.content: The user keeps a travel power bank in the first drawer beneath the desk.
The user packed three pairs of shoes for a two-night trip but wore only one pair.
For the next two-night trip, the user packed only one pair of walking shoes and reduced the bag's weight.
On a trip when the user forgot a charging cable, they bought a new one after arrival.
Before the next trip, the user checked charging items against a photo and packed all of them.
The user packed toiletries on the departure day and arrived 15 minutes late at the meeting place.
The next time, the user closed the bag the night before and departed on time.
The user's older sister considers it safer to pack an extra cable even for a short trip to avoid charging problems.
When creating a travel preparation list, confirm the trip length and actual activities with the user.
The local agent cannot establish what the next trip requires from the luggage used on the previous trip alone.
The user keeps a picnic mat on the bottom shelf of the entrance storage cabinet.
On a day the user went to the riverside, they sat in a place without shade and moved after an hour.
At the next outdoor meal, the user chose a place near a large tree and stayed for two hours.
On a hot day when the user brought only one bottle of water, they bought another drink partway through the outing.
On the next outing, the user brought two small bottles of water after freezing them.
When meeting their maternal uncle at a park, the user and the uncle waited at different entrances for 15 minutes.
For the next meeting, the user sent a photo of the entrance sign, and they met at the same place.
For a park meeting, the user's maternal uncle prefers an entrance that requires less walking from the parking area.
When making an outdoor plan, confirm the exact entrance and an alternative location in case of rain.
Some park restrooms and drinking fountains may be closed seasonally.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate preparation domains: short-trip packing and outdoor outings. Each records lessons from prior mishaps, later adaptations, stored equipment, family preferences, and planning constraints. Their planning guidance shares a context-sensitive approach but requires different details for travel and park activities.
